audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty text repeatedly claims Mel has no hard CC. Solar Snare (E) is a root at 1000 range on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s.
audit.why: Irelia's whole pattern is dash-in; a 1000-range root is the single thing that stops it, so calling it absent inverts the lane.
audit.corrected: Favoured 4/10, but the difficulty is timing: dash after Solar Snare is spent, never into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 described as 'a strong teamfight beam' that does nothing; Golden Eclipse is global (25000 range) and scales with Overwhelm stacks.
audit.why: It kills after the trade, not during it — the practical advice is to stop farming at low HP, which the current text omits entirely.
audit.corrected: Golden Eclipse 120/100/80, global, cashes every Overwhelm stack she has put on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ability name 'Reflected Radiance' in spikes[0] and wants.foe[1]; the ability is Rebuttal (W). Rebuttal's projectile-reflection is never tied to Irelia's own projectiles.
audit.why: Both Irelia's E (Bladesurge blades) and R (Vanguard's Edge) carry the projectile flag, and Rebuttal reflects projectiles and prevents damage for its duration on a 38/35/33/29/26s cooldown. That is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it was unstated.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal reflects your E and R and blanks damage — bait it, count the 26s at rank 5, then commit. Solar Snare (E, 11s to 9s) is her only lockdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Searing Brilliance (P) execute threshold and the bonus-projectile auto reset were never mentioned.
audit.why: Overwhelm stacks infinitely and converts into a threshold execute; the auto after any ability carries up to nine projectiles, which is the burst tell.

edits.before: Mel is a poke mage with no dash and no hard crowd control, so once you hit level 2 with Q you already threaten to close the distance and punish her before she can kite away. Her passive/shield abilities mitigate some damage but don't stop your combo, and she has to play at max range just to survive early trades. You can freely contest CS and push your advantage in short skirmishes.
edits.after: Mel is a poke mage with no dash, but Solar Snare is a real root at 1000 range on an 11-second cooldown, so respect it before you commit. Once you hit level 2 with Q you threaten to close the gap the moment that root is spent. Rebuttal blanks your damage entirely while it holds — bait it, never poke into it. Contest CS on minions you can dash to and win the short skirmishes.

edits.before: From levels 3-5 your combo damage and gap-closing keep you heavily favored, since Mel's kit is built around sustained poke and shielding rather than dueling. Level 6 gives her a strong teamfight ultimate, but it does nothing to help her survive a 1v1 all-in, so the power spike is largely irrelevant to your lane matchup. You should keep pressuring her whenever she's forced to last-hit in range of your dash.
edits.after: From levels 3-5 your E-stun into four stacked autos beats her poke pattern, since Rebuttal is 33 seconds at rank 3 and Solar Snare is the only thing that holds you off. Level 6 does not save her in a duel, but Golden Eclipse is global and cashes every Overwhelm stack she has landed on you, so recall low rather than farming at low health. Keep pressuring her whenever she last-hits in dash range.

edits.before: Even with a completed build, Mel lacks any hard escape or disengage, meaning a well-timed Trinity Force dash from Irelia can isolate and kill her in skirmishes before her team reacts. Her scaling comes from poke damage and teamfight utility, not personal survivability, so she remains vulnerable to dive comps. As long as you don't walk into a full peel setup, you keep winning direct confrontations.
edits.after: Even with a completed build, Mel's only personal out is Rebuttal — 26 seconds at rank 5, damage immunity plus a movement-speed burst — so open by making her spend it, then dash in and E-stun once it fades. Her scaling is poke and the Overwhelm execute, not survivability, so she stays vulnerable to a dive. As long as you don't walk into full peel, you win direct confrontations.
